cells.tense: You're standing here with the work in your hands, and you can see its shape clearly.
cells.ask: Let one thing you've been carrying be finished — and when it's done, let it go where someone who watched you hold it can see.
cells.core:
Here you can see the pattern under a thing and tend it without naming every piece. You give it form, and it grows — the eye and the hand moving together, patient, unforced. That's what's happening now. You're holding two things that both need you without dropping either, and nothing is being forced.

Being seen doesn't have to be earned. It's what happens when the tending is done and you let it be done — the release that comes from finishing, not from giving up. Let one finished thing go where someone can watch it leave your hands. You'll feel the difference between setting it down and losing it.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending what grows, and you can let it be finished.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: where you see the shape of how things work, stripped of the particulars

cells.tense: You're already living in a future where it's gone wrong, bracing for it before it arrives.
cells.ask: Before you plan the next move, finish one thing you already started — let what you imagined be actually done before you imagine the next.
cells.core:
At its steadiness, you can see how something works and tend it from the pattern rather than the details — hold the shape while it takes and let it grow at its own speed. There's a care in that which doesn't exhaust.

What's happening instead is that you see the pattern so clearly you start managing every branch of it ahead of time, and the tending turns into gripping. You're not growing the thing anymore — you're guarding it from a future you've already drawn. Real care, gone tight. The way back is the satisfaction of having made something real — the vision fully felt, not forecast. Finish one thing. Let it be done, and let that be enough for today.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a future instead of finishing what's in front of you.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: where you see the shape of how things work, stripped of the particulars

cells.tense: You're standing at a doorway you already walked through, still deciding whether to tend what's on the other side.
cells.ask: Pick one thing worth tending and stay with it past the point where you'd normally go quiet — let hope be the thing that keeps you there.
cells.core:
At its best this is the eye and the hand together — you see how something works and tend it from the shape rather than the details, patient, holding the pattern while it takes.

The eye is here and the hand isn't. You see the mechanism, you know what would grow, and you're not picking anything up. What's gone quiet isn't the sight — it's the willingness to keep hoping the thing will actually come. What keeps you here is the simple refusal to quit: not forcing, just not leaving. Choose one thing. Keep showing up for it past where you usually stop.
cells.sheetLine: You see what would grow. You're not tending it.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care

cells.tense: The pen is already moving while you tell yourself you're not the one holding it.
cells.ask: Tell one person about something you do for them out of care, and let it be seen as care rather than just handled.
cells.core:
When it's working, your eye for pattern does the work — you see how things hold together and you tend them accordingly, from the shape, and people feel steadied without quite knowing why.

The tending is happening now. Who's doing it is sitting on the table unclaimed, and you carry it as though it were simply the way things are. A smaller thing than you'd think is the way back: the care becomes visible to someone, and their seeing it makes it real in a way you can't manage alone. Name one thing you do for someone and call it what it is. You don't have to defend it or explain it. Just let it be seen.
